_why: Tests that never run because an import is missing. Baselined 2026-08-06 while fixing the three-day red main, NOT blessed: a skipped test is not a passing test. This number may only go DOWN. scripts/check_dependency_skips.py fails the build if it rises or if a new dependency joins the list.

_recovering_these.shapely: In requirements.txt (2.1.2) but not requirements-test.txt. Ships manylinux wheels; most likely genuinely installable, so these 13 are the cheapest to win back.
_recovering_these.numpy + matplotlib + PIL: matplotlib is the missing one (numpy and pillow are already in the CI closure). requirements.txt pins 3.11.0.
_recovering_these.icontract: Declared in NO runtime requirements file — only scripts/requirements-maintenance.txt. services/flood_truth.py carries a _FakeIcontract no-op fallback, so its postconditions are inert in CI, locally AND in the deployed service. These 5 tests assert those postconditions fire, so they have never once run. Worth its own decision: either make icontract a real dependency of the service that advertises contracts, or stop advertising them.
